audit_scope.description: This batch covers both EL and CL logic: EVM opcode behavior (EIP-4399 PREVRANDAO), precompile address allocation (EIP-7587), transaction monitoring RPC (EIP-8072), fork choice with inclusion lists (EIP-7805, Capella), beacon state fork transitions (Gloas), voluntary exit signature validation (EIP-7044), client metrics (EIP-2159), and network upgrade coordination (EIP-8081).

misclassified_entities.reason: In EIP-8072 security subgraph, 'Ethereum Node' is modeled as external but is actually the system under audit providing the RPC service. It is the EL node itself sending notifications to the user application.

In EIP-4399 security subgraph, 'RANDAO-Dependent Contract' is a smart contract running inside the EVM, which is part of the EL under audit. It is a consumer of the PREVRANDAO opcode, not an external entity sending data into the system.

In EIP-8081, 'EIP Author/Champion' is a governance participant in the network upgrade process, not a runtime external entity that sends data into EL or CL at execution time. This is a process-level actor, not a trust boundary actor.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer via P2P (Beacon Blocks)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated P2P network peers can send arbitrary signed beacon blocks. All block content must be fully validated including ancestry, temporal, finalization, and state transition checks.

trusted_external_entities.name: Execution Engine via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Authenticated via JWT between CL and EL. However, responses (e.g., is_inclusion_list_satisfied result, payload validity) must be treated as data requiring validation. A faulty EL could falsely report inclusion list satisfaction.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Engine API (newPayload, forkchoiceUpdated with PayloadAttributes including withdrawals)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Authenticated via JWT. CL provides RANDAO values, withdrawal lists, and fork choice updates to EL. Data content (e.g., RANDAO mix in mixHash field, withdrawal sequences) requires validation by EL.

trusted_external_entities.name: Inclusion List Committee Member via P2P
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P gossip (inclusion list topic, on_inclusion_list handler)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Committee members broadcast signed inclusion lists over unauthenticated P2P. Lists must be validated for correct committee assignment, valid signatures, and timing (before VIEW_FREEZE_CUTOFF). Malicious committee members could submit conflicting or late lists.

trusted_external_entities.name: User/DApp via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated public RPC endpoint. Users can submit arbitrary transactions and subscription requests. Full parameter validation required (mutual exclusion of tx/hash, transaction validity). Resource exhaustion via long-lived subscriptions is a concern.

trusted_external_entities.name: Layer 2 Rollup (RIP Precompile Deployer)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: L2 rollups deploying RIP precompiles are independent systems outside L1 control. Address space reservation is a governance mechanism; L2s may deploy conflicting precompiles. On L1, calls to the reserved range must be handled correctly (no collision with EIP precompiles).

trusted_external_entities.name: Smart Contract via EVM CALL
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: EVM CALL opcode targeting precompile addresses
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any contract can call precompile addresses. The EVM must correctly route calls based on address range (EIP 0x01-0xff vs RIP 0x100-0x1ff) without collision.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Proposer (Validator) via P2P
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Proposers control their RANDAO reveal and can bias randomness by 1 bit per slot through selective withholding. Proposers are untrusted for RANDAO integrity; the system accepts this limited bias as a known tradeoff.

trusted_external_entities.name: Validator Operator via Signed Voluntary Exit
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Anyone holding a signed voluntary exit can submit it. Signature must be verified against fixed Capella fork domain. Cross-fork replay is possible by design but considered safe since exits only initiate the exit process without transferring funds.

trusted_external_entities.name: Prometheus Server via HTTP
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External monitoring system scraping metrics. Unauthenticated by default. Exposes operational state (sync status, peer count, block height) which could provide attack intelligence. Should be network-restricted.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Peer Node via devp2p
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Archetypal EL attack vector. Malicious peers can send invalid blocks, transactions, or attempt eclipse attacks. All data from P2P peers requires full validation.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Validator via Beacon P2P
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Archetypal CL attack vector. Can propose invalid blocks, submit conflicting attestations, or attempt censorship. Subject to slashing conditions.

trusted_external_entities.name: MEV-Boost Relay via External API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Archetypal CL external service attack vector. Could provide incorrect block data, censor transactions, or perform denial of service. Particularly relevant given Gloas builder registry introduction.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full block validation required: ancestry verification, temporal validity (slot <= current slot), finalization constraints, state transition execution. Block must not be accepted into fork choice store without passing all checks.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Engine API response (is_inclusion_list_satisfied, payload validity status)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: CL must handle EL responses defensively. A false is_inclusion_list_satisfied response could allow censoring proposers to bypass inclusion list enforcement. EL payload validity must be cross-checked.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Engine API (newPayload with RANDAO in mixHash, forkchoiceUpdated with withdrawals in PayloadAttributes)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: EL must validate RANDAO value range (>2^64 confirms PoS context), withdrawal sequence constraints (max 16, ordered by index), and payload structural integrity. JWT authentication required but content validation essential.
Must validate: committee membership, BLS signature, timing (before VIEW_FREEZE_CUTOFF at 75% of slot), transaction content validity. Late inclusion lists must be rejected.

Full parameter validation: mutual exclusion of transaction/hash parameters, standard transaction validation if tx provided, resource limits on subscription count/duration. Privacy consideration: node operators can observe monitoring patterns.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: EVM CALL to precompile address (0x01-0xff for EIP, 0x100-0x1ff for RIP)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Address range resolution must correctly distinguish EIP vs RIP precompile spaces. No address collision between ranges. On L1, calls to RIP range addresses should behave as calls to empty accounts.

Proposer can bias RANDAO by 1 bit through selective withholding (forfeiting rewards). System accepts this as known limitation. Applications using PREVRANDAO must implement commit-reveal with multi-epoch delays. RANDAO value is propagated to EL via mixHash.

Signature must be verified against fixed Capella fork domain (CAPELLA_FORK_VERSION). Cross-fork replay is acceptable by design. Exits only initiate exit process, no fund transfer. Post-EIP-7044, exits signed with non-Capella domains must be rejected.

Endpoint should be network-restricted to authorized monitoring systems only. Exposed metrics (sync status, peer count, block height) provide operational intelligence that could aid attack timing. No authentication mechanism defined in EIP-2159.
All blocks and transactions from P2P must be fully validated. Eclipse attack mitigations required. Invalid data must be rejected without corrupting local state.
All proposals and attestations must be validated against consensus rules. Conflicting attestations trigger slashing. Censorship attempts mitigated by inclusion list enforcement (EIP-7805).

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: MEV-Boost relay API (block bids, payload delivery)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Relay-provided blocks must be fully validated. Relay data is untrusted. Particularly relevant with Gloas builder registry: builders onboarded via deposits must be verified through withdrawal credential classification and prior-signature checks to prevent unauthorized builder registration.
